comment_text.ja46:1.1: A lazy groundskeeper asks the monkeys in the park to water the trees in his absence. They set to work with all good cheer. However, misconstruing the instructions, they pull up each tree to examine the size of the roots before watering, thus ruining the park despite their good intentions.
comment_text.ja46:1.2: The verse plays on two meanings of attha. In the opening line, attha is “meaning, basis” (as per Snp 1.8:1.1 or AN 5.169:3.1), and it is glossed āyatane kāraṇe (“reason, cause”). Here it means “good, benefit” and is glossed vuḍḍhi (“growth”).

translation_text.ja46:0.4: Spoiling the Park: a past life story
translation_text.ja46:1.1: Surely not with one who misunderstands the meaning
translation_text.ja46:1.2: does good conduct lead to happiness.
